challenges and climate change, there is growing
interest in eco-friendly foods that have less impact
on the environment. The following foods eaten in
various regions of the world are gaining attention
as sustainable foods for the future.
False Bananas
ⓐ에티오피아는 그것의 커피 재배로 유명한데, 유망한
미래 작물인 엔셋(enset)이 번성하는 지역이기도 하다.
Enset, also known as “false banana,” is a close
relative of the banana. The fruit of the plant isn’t
safe to eat, but the stems and roots can be
processed and used to make bread. Approximately
20 million people (A)[rely on / do without] this
plant for food in Ethiopia, but it is almost unknown
outside of the country. Scientists anticipate that this
crop has the potential to feed more than 100
million people in a warming world, establishing
itself as a new fundamental food for the future.
Cacti
Native to the deserts of both North and South
America, cacti are a fundamental food in Latin
American communities, where the flat pads are
often stirred and served with eggs or in salads and
tacos. There are over 1,500 species of cacti, and
many of them are safe to eat. Cacti are rich in
fiber, vitamins, and other nutrients. Cacti’s ability to
thrive in dry and harsh environments makes them a
(B)[crucial / dispensable] crop in the face of climate
change.
Seaweed
Seaweed is a type of plant that typically flourishes
along rocky coasts around the world. This plant
offers a range of flavors that are used in a variety
of dishes, including soups, salads, and snacks.
Seaweed is mostly eaten in Korea, Japan, and
China, but it is becoming more common in other
parts of the world. Seaweed, gaining attention for
(C)[aggravating / addressing] soil degradation, is
packed with fiber, essential vitamins, and minerals,
offering numerous health benefits.

Universal design suggests that design be as
flexible as possible so that it can accommodate
diverse needs and a wide range of individual
preferences. This could involve providing a variety
of options for customization or adding adjustable
features to a product.
Take a look at the scissors, the computer mouse,
and the desk pictured below. Do you notice how
they differ from the more common types of
scissors, mice, and desks? They are all designed for
left-handed people. Without them, about 10% of
the world’s population, who are left-handed, would
find these simple products difficult to use.
The height-adjustable desk is also a good example
of a universal design that accommodates a wide
range of individual preferences and abilities. If the
desk is too high or too low, the users can adjust it
to the heights they want. If desired, the user can
work while standing. A wheelchair user is also able
to use the desk at a comfortable height.
